name: King of Arpad
overview: The King of Arpad was a male monarch known primarily for his defeat by the Assyrian empire, as recorded in 2 Kings 19:13. Beyond this, Scripture does not provide details about his tribe or additional personal notes. His role is noted within the context of Assyrian military campaigns against various kings.
namesAndTitles: The title 'King of Arpad' straightforwardly identifies him as the ruler of the city-state of Arpad. The name itself means 'king of Arpad' and is a descriptive title rather than a personal name, highlighting his position rather than individual identity. This title is referenced specifically in 2 Kings 19:13.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships or connections for the King of Arpad beyond his role as a monarch defeated by Assyria. There are no listed relatives or tribal affiliations associated with him in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: The King of Arpad serves as a representative of the defeated kings who opposed Assyrian expansion, illustrating the sovereignty and judgment of God over earthly powers. His mention underscores the historical reality of Assyria’s dominance during the period and serves as a backdrop to the narrative involving God's deliverance of His people. His defeat contributes to the biblical theme of God’s control over nations and kings.
